stem: When coordinating post-transplant bone-health care, which supplement aligns with standard references for osteopenia or osteoporosis prevention?

options.text: No supplements because transplantation prevents bone loss
High-dose iron supplements as the sole bone-health therapy
Calcium supplementation is contraindicated in all transplant recipients

explanation.rationale_correct: Prevention and treatment of osteopenia or osteoporosis includes calcium and vitamin D supplements along with other therapies such as bisphosphonates and exercise when indicated.

rationale_incorrect.B: Recipients are at increased bone-loss risk and may require supplementation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Calcium and vitamin D are the referenced supplements rather than iron alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Calcium and vitamin D supplementation is recommended rather than contraindicated for all recipients.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 6, Noninfectious Diseases → Preserve bone health → Prevent or treat osteopenia/osteoporosis

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).

notes: Source-first item. Calcium/vitamin D supplementation angle distinct from osteopenia exercise teaching (cctc-1047) and DEXA interval recall (cctc-3105); anchor verified on Cupples p. 322.

stem: A post-transplant recipient with declining bone mineral density on DEXA asks about medication options. Which therapy aligns with standard bone-health references?

options.text: Bisphosphonates to reverse bone loss and increase bone mass
No bone medications because immunosuppression strengthens bone
Routine daily bone marrow biopsy instead of medication
Bisphosphonates are permanently contraindicated after every transplant

explanation.rationale_correct: Treatment of osteopenia or osteoporosis may include bisphosphonates to reverse bone loss and increase bone mass, along with calcium, vitamin D, and exercise.

rationale_incorrect.B: Immunosuppression contributes to bone loss rather than preventing it.
rationale_incorrect.C: Bisphosphonates are pharmacologic therapy rather than routine daily biopsy.
rationale_incorrect.D: Bisphosphonates are treatment options when indicated rather than being universally contraindicated.

stem: A coordinator schedules bone-health follow-up after starting a new osteoporosis medication. When should DEXA be repeated per standard references?

options.text: Six months after initiating the new drug treatment to assess effectiveness
Only once at thirty years post-transplant
Daily DEXA scans for the first week only

explanation.rationale_correct: DEXA screening includes rechecking six months after initiating a new drug treatment to assess effectiveness, in addition to baseline, six-month post-transplant, and periodic reassessment.

rationale_incorrect.B: Medication effectiveness is monitored with repeat DEXA rather than omitting reassessment.
rationale_incorrect.C: Six-month post-treatment initiation reassessment is recommended rather than decennial-only scanning.
rationale_incorrect.D: Six-month reassessment after new therapy is referenced rather than daily scanning.

stem: A coordinator is updating post-transplant bone-health teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Calcium and vitamin D supplements may be used to prevent or treat osteopenia or osteoporosis.
Bisphosphonates may reverse bone loss and increase bone mass.
Exercise is not recommended for transplant recipients with bone disease.
DEXA may be rechecked six months after initiating a new bone medication.

explanation.rationale_correct: Calcium and vitamin D supplementation, bisphosphonate therapy, and six-month post-treatment DEXA reassessment are supported. Statement III is false because exercise is listed as part of bone-health management.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—DEXA may be rechecked six months after starting new bone therapy.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false because exercise is recommended.
